Traditional dignities of your planets

In classical astrology (William Lilly, Christian Astrology, 1647) a planet is stronger in its domicile and exaltation, and weaker in its detriment and fall. Planets that are in none of those four conditions do not appear here.
<h3 class=\"ca-h\">Tus aspectos más fuer:
Your strongest aspects

Aspects are the angles between planets. On the wheel, blue lines are flowing aspects and red ones are tense. For Lilly, the sextile and trine favor union, the square is a tension that can still be resolved, and the opposition is the strongest clash; a conjunction is good or bad depending on how well the planets that join get along.
